# Sabrahmaka Sutta (Iti 106 (It 4.7 PTS It 109))

**ID:** Iti 106 (It 4.7 PTS It 109)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Sabrahmaka Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sabrahmaka Sutta* is the seventh discourse of the fourth chapter (the *Catukkanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka*, located at PTS It 109. In this discourse, the Buddha explains why families where parents are venerated within the home are said to live with Brahmā, with the early teachers, and with those worthy of gifts. Mother and father are characterized as the Brahmās and first teachers of their children because of their great care, nurture, and guidance in introducing children to the world.

 Automated text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus corroborates extensive textual sharing with AN 4.63 (segments §2.1–6.4 aligning with AN §63.0.3–63.5.4) and AN 3.31 (§2.2–6.4 aligning with AN §31.1.1–31.4.4) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus detects verse reuse across several commentary collections, including the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā*, *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, and identifies cross-linguistic textual alignments with the Sanskrit *Avadānaśataka*, the Tibetan *Pitṛmātṛ-sūtra* (D0315, *pha ma'i mdo*), and the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus]. None of the secondary literature passages matched in the dossier directly examine this specific sutta, as they refer to homonymous vocabulary or to different texts [Lamotte 1994].
